FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Pneumatic Fluid Power Systems Sectional Committee, had been approved by the Basic and Production Engineering Division Council. In pneumatic fluid power systems, power is transmitted and controlled through air under pressure within a circuit. Where lubrication of the air media is desired, compressed air lubricators are components designed to inlroduce the required quantity of lubricant into the air stream. This standard specifies the requirements for compressed air lubricators used in pneumatic fluid power systems. The requirements laid down in this standard shall be included in the supplier's literature. The aim of the standard in addition to others is: a) b) To facilitate the comparison of lubricators by standardizing test methods and presentation of test data; and To assist in the proper application of lubricators in compressed air systems.

The tests specified are intcndcd to allow comparison between different types of lubricators; and they are not production tests to be carried out on each lubricator manufactured. The units from IS 10005 : 1994 `SI units and recommendations for the use of their multiples and of certain other units (second revision)' are generally used in pneumatic fluid power systems, in particular:
a)

Gauge pressure exprcsscd in kilopascals (bar); Temperature expressed in degrees Celsius; and Flow rate, expressed in cubic decimetres per second (ANR).

b) c)

While preparing this standard, considerable assistance has been derived from the following standards issued by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO): IS0 6301-l : 1997 `Pneumatic fluid power - Compressed~air~lubricators-Part to be included in supplier's literature and product-marking requirements' IS0 6301-2 : 1997 `Pneumatic fluid power - Compressed air lubricators determine the main characteristics to be included in supplier's literature' This standard is technically equivalent to above international standards. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be grounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rowcling off numerical values (revised)`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded ofT value should be the same as that ~of the specified value in this standard. 1 : Main characteristics Part 2 : Test methods to

1 SCOPE IS No. - -

Title

1.1 This standard lays down the evaluation parameters for air lubricators used in pneumatic fluid power system. 1.2 This standard is appkdbk to compressed air lubricators, manufactured from light alloys (aluminium, etc), zinc diecast alloys, brass, steel and plastic with a rated pressure of up to 1 600 kPa (16 bar) and a maximum temperature of 80�C. 2 REFERENCES 2.1 The following Indian Standards contain provisions which through reference in this text, constitute provisions of this standard. At the time of publication, the editions indicated were valid. All standards are subject to revision, and parties to agreements based on this standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent editions of the standards indicated below.
IS No. Title

14740 : 1999

Pneumatic fluid power - Components using compressible fluids - Determination of flow rate characteristics

3 DEFINITIONS For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given in IS 10416 shall apply together with the following: 3.1 Compressed Air Lubricator-Component designed to introduce controlled quantities of lubricant into the compressed air stream. There are two kinds of compressed air lubricators based upon two principles of operation, as defined in 3.1.1 and 3.1.2. 3.1.1 Non-recirculating Lubricator-Lubricator which injects into the air flow all the oil passing through the oil feed mechanism. 3.1.2 Recirculating Lubricator-Lubricator which injects into the air flow only a portion of the oil observed passing through the oil feed mechanism. 3.2 Rated Pressure--Pressure confirmed through testing, at which a component or piping is designed to operate for a number of repetitions sufficient to assure adequate service life. 3.3 Minimum Operating Flow for a LubricatorMinimum flow-rate which, with the minimum oil level in the reservoir, provides an oil feed and atomization of the lubricant with a theoretical concentration when the oil feed mechanism is set at the maximum. 4 TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS

The rated pressure shall be verified using the test procedure specified in 7.
4.1.4 Range of Operating Temperature 4.1.4.1 The temperature range in which the material

and the operation of the lubricator are not impaired shall be stated. 4.1.4.2 Alternate combinations of constant maximum operating pressure and temperature ratings when optional designs may require a different rating shall be specified. 4.2 Particular Requirements 4.2.1 The data -provided by the supplier shall assist the user in selecting the compressed air lubricator which is~best suited for the particular application.

The pressure drop at additional inlet pressures, such as described in IS 5107 or elsewhere, may also be recorded. Results shall be presented in either graphical or tabular form. of Oil Flow

Leakage across the port threads may not constitute a failure unless caused by a fracture or crack. ' 7.7 The proposed rated pressure will be verified ifall three samples pass the test. 7.8 Where a unit or sub-assembly in the unit (for example reservoir/sight glass) is constructed of different materials, the highest appropriate factor should be used. The applied pressure may be restricted to the area of the interface between the different materials. 7.9 Where the design of the `pressure-containing envelope is covered by a statutory pressure vessel code the requirements of that code take' precedence over the requirements stated in this standard. 8 FLOW RATE TESTS

7J The test shall be performed on three random samples with a proposed rated pressure for the product.

7.2 In this test, the product-sealing means can be mo-dified to prevent leakage and allow structural failure~to occur; but modifications must not increase the structural strength of the pressure-containing envelope. 7.3 Fill samples with a liquid of viscosity that-does not exceed IS0 VG 32 according to 2.2 and Table 1 of IS 9466 and install them in the temperature environment described in 6.1.
7.4 Alter stabilizing the temperature, pressurize slowly to ~a level of 1.5 times the proposed rated pressure. Hold at this level for,2 min and observe for leakage or failure (as defined in 7.6).

described in Fig. 1, Table 3 and 5.3 of IS 14740. 8.2 The measuring tubes shall comply fully with those described in Fig. 3, Table 4 and 5.4 and 5.5 of IS 14740. 8.3 The oil feed control shall be set to zero, and there shall be no oil in the reservoir.
NOTE - The purpose of this operation is to reduce the chance of contamination of the flow measuring device.

7.5 If there is no leakage or failure, increase the pressure by approximately half of its proposed rating. Hold~at this pressure for 2 min and observe for leakage or failure (as defined in 7.6). If there is still no leakage or failure in terms of the following units: a)

8.4 Each series of results obtained for a specified test condition shall be recorded as soon as a steady-state condition has been reached. Recording shall be carried out with care and with a sufllciently slow period of change in conditions to avoid a drift in the steadystate characteristic. A periodic check shall be made to verify that no pressure intakes of measuring instruments are blocked by solid or liquid particles. 8.5 Set the inlet pressure to test levels of 250 kPa, 630 kRa, 1 000 kPa (2.5 bar, 6.3 bar, 10 bar) or at the rated pressure if different from 1000 kPa (10 bar). Adjust the inlet pressure during the flow-rate te.st to maintain it constant. 8.6 Begin circulating air through the test circuit, recording flow rate and pressure drop, upto a maximum flow rate corresponding to a pressure drop equal to the lesser of 80 kPa (0.8 bar) or 20 percent of the inlet pressure. Then record flow rate and pressure drop with flow rate decreasing to zero. 8.7 Results shall be taken from the mean of the increasing or decreasing flow rate data and presented in accordance with 4.2.2, Fig. 2 and Table 1 recording

IS 14876: 2000 theport size and the type of lubricator, or according to Table 1, where the flow-rate at which the pressure drop is 5 percent of the inlet pressure is tabulated. 9 TEST PROCEDURE TO ESTABLISH MINIMUM OPERATING FLOW THE 9.6 Continue the test trials until an oil delivery time between drops exceeds 2 min (or more if possible). The amount of time between drops after 2 or more minutes, and the corresponding air flow rate, is the last data required. lf this data point is not obtainable before 15 mm between drops, discontinue testing and use the last data obtainable. 9.7 Prepare a graph as shown in Fig. 3, where the theoretical concentration line passes through the origin, and a) the point of 1 drop/mm at 5 dm3/s for nonrecirculating lubricators; or b) the point of 1 drop/min at 0.5 dm3/s for recirculating lubricators.

9.1 Install the lubricator into the test circuit as described in 8.1 and 8.2, however delete the downstream pressure-measuring tube and locate the flowmeter only in the upstream location. 9.2 The reservoir shall be partially filled with a liquid of viscosity not less than IS0 VG 32 according to 2.2 and Table 1 of IS 9466 to a liquid level approximately l/4 of the reservoir capacity as determined in 10. 9.3 Set the oil feed mechanism to its maximum open position and maintain this throughout the test. 9.4 With the supply pressure held constant at 630 kPa (6.3 bar) (or the rated pressure if lower), sufliciently open the flow control valve in the test circuit to generate an oil delivery of at least 5 drops per minute, as observed in the sight dome. Record the time interval between drops and the corresponding air flow rate after the system has stabilized. 9.5 Perform a series of test trials with progressively reduced air flow rates, adjusting the flow control valve in the test circuit for each trial. Record the time interval between drops and the corresponding air flow rate for each trial. Maintain the supply pressure constant at 630 kFa (6.3 bar) (or the rated pressure~if lower) during each trial.

Plot the data measured during testing onto this graph (convert the data measurement from "time between drops" to "drops per minute").
NOTE - At low flow rates the theoretical concentration line is close to the air flow rate axis.

9.8 The minimum operating flow-will be the air flow rate corresponding to the intersection of a curve drawn through the data points with the theoretical concentration line, shown as example Y in Fig. 3. If the curve drawn through the data points does not intersect the theoretical concentration line, the minimum operating flow rate will be the air flow rate measured at the last data points obtainable, shown as example X in Fig. 3.

IS 14876 : 2000 10 CAPACITY RESERVOIR MEASUREMENT OF THE The manufacturer's or supplier's model or type number;

10.1 This test method determines the capacity of a lubricator reservoir. 10.2 Select three random samples of complete lubricators from normal -production units, for each size of lubricator reservoir. 10.3 With the lubricator completely assembled, measure the amount of liquid necessary to fill the reservoir from the level 2 mm above the bottom of the pick-up tube to the maximum fill level marked by the manufacturer. 10.4 Determine the average for each group of samples. This will be the rated reservoir capacity for a given reservoir size. 11 MARKING 11.1 Each compressed air lubricator shall be marked with the following information: a) The manufacturer's trade-mark; or supplier's name or
